cases.question: I have a new phone and one unused backup code. What should I do?

response.answer: If you are replacing your authenticator device, you should use one unused backup code to sign in, and then register the new authenticator in your account security settings. If you have no backup codes left, you must contact the IT service desk to verify your identity and have MFA enrollment reset.

sources.title: Recover multi-factor authentication after replacing a phone
sources.text: When the authenticator device is lost or replaced, use one unused backup code to sign in, then register the new authenticator in account security settings. If no backup codes remain, the IT service desk must verify identity and reset MFA enrollment. Do not disable MFA or share one-time codes.

cases.question: How do I connect my laptop to student wifi?

response.answer: To connect your laptop to the student wireless network, choose "Campus-Student" in your wireless settings. You must then authenticate using your full student email address and your campus password. It is important to validate the certificate against the profile published in the student portal, and you should not accept any unexpected certificate. If a saved profile keeps failing, you should forget the network and install the current campus profile.

sources.title: Connect to the student wireless network

cases.question: Can IT extend my deadline if my assignment upload fails?

response.answer: If you have a deadline problem, you should contact the instructor. The IT department cannot extend a deadline or guarantee acceptance for failed assignment uploads.

sources.title: Fix a failed assignment file upload
sources.text: The learning platform accepts PDF and ZIP assignment files up to 20 MB unless the instructor states otherwise. Rename the file using letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores; retry in a current browser. For a deadline problem, contact the instructor. IT cannot extend a deadline or guarantee acceptance.

cases.question: I entered my password into a fake login link. What is the next step?

response.answer: If you entered your credentials into a fake login link, you should reset your campus password from the trusted portal and contact the IT service desk immediately. The handbook also advises using the mail client's Report phishing action for suspicious links or emails, and if a device ran an attachment, disconnect it from the network and ask IT for help.

sources.title: Report a suspicious sign-in link or email
sources.text: Do not open suspicious links, download attachments, or enter credentials. Use the mail client Report phishing action. If credentials were entered, reset the campus password from the trusted portal and contact the IT service desk immediately. If a device ran an attachment, disconnect it from the network and ask IT for help.

cases.question: Can you issue me a refund right now for a print job with blank pages?

response.answer: To request credit back for a charged print job with blank or damaged pages, you must request a print-credit review in the print portal within 48 hours. You will need to include the job ID, printer ID, and a description of the failure. Please note that the assistant cannot issue credit or approve refunds.
